page: Amazon Web Services r8id.large is a memory-optimized Nitro-based virtual server designed for workloads needing a high memory-to-vCPU allocation paired with fast local scratch storage. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it is powered by an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor clocked at 3.9 GHz, providing 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from a single physical core with hyper-threading enabled. The compute layer includes support for advanced instructions such as AVX-512, AMX, AES, and SHA_NI. The instance is provisioned with 16 GB of high-speed DDR5 system memory (8 GB per vCPU) and includes a dedicated 118 GB local NVMe SSD, while networking is configured with a 1 Gbps baseline bandwidth. No physical GPU accelerators are included.

Benchmark measurements reflect the constraints of its two-vCPU hardware footprint. Single-core performance is robust, evidenced by a strong Geekbench single-core score of 2,169.0, single-threaded gzip compression of 34.32 GB/sec, and bzip3 decompression of 14.43 GB/sec. Conversely, overall multithreaded capacity is constrained by the limited core count, registering bottom-tier outcomes in stress-ng multi-core (2,159.19) and PassMark CPU tests (4,078.74). Uncached memory bandwidth for large 256 MB blocks reaches 21.81 GB/sec for reads and 17.01 GB/sec for writes. In application-level benchmarks, the instance delivers 3.81 million operations per second in Redis SET operations and 5.29 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

Cost efficiency for the r8id.large is centered on its resource ratio rather than raw aggregate throughput. It offers an economical entry point for applications requiring DDR5 memory capacity alongside local NVMe scratch space without paying for higher core counts. The main architectural tradeoff is the small CPU allocation, which bottlenecks parallel workloads like multi-threaded compilation and heavy database operations. This instance fits memory-centric services, in-memory caches, light key-value databases, local-storage ETL staging tasks, and single-threaded batch processing.
description: Amazon Web Services r8id.large is a memory-optimized virtual instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, featuring an x86_64 Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor operating at 3.9 GHz. It supplies 2 dedicated vCPUs from 1 physical core, 16 GB of DDR5 RAM, and bundled local storage consisting of a 118 GB NVMe SSD, alongside a 1 Gbps baseline network interface. The instance does not feature a GPU. Benchmark testing demonstrates strong single-threaded throughput, registering 2,169.0 in Geekbench single-core and 34.32 GB/sec in gzip compression, though aggregate multithreaded and parallel compute scores remain limited due to the 2 vCPU profile. With an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio and high-speed local disk storage, the r8id.large is engineered for memory-heavy, low-core-demand workloads such as Redis caching, small transactional databases, data ingestion pipelines, and local caching servers.
